recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant Parameters prose for FHIR-17406 unless a future work-group decision changes the intended semantics; any future correction to the parameters-fullUrl extension definition belongs in the FHIR Extension Pack rather than this core checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-17406 was Published with resolution Persuasive. It asked FHIR-I to add discussion of resource id uniqueness inside Parameters, specifically whether repeated parameter.resource entries with the same resource type/id can be presumed to be the same resource or same version.
initial_application: The issue was applied by svn revision 13943, preserved as git commit fe6dcf86ed15f9323e86654a929fd4bc3352dddf, which added the Parameters Names and Identifiers table to source/parameters/parameters-notes.xml. Later adjacent commits for FHIR-17509 and FHIR-17405 added the reference-resolution row and fullUrl-extension qualifier in the same table.
additional_context: Parameters is an active current-build resource through source/fhir.ini. Current surrounding source in types.html and references.html confirms that internal id scope and fragment-reference resolution break at Parameters.parameter.resource. Bundle source still defines the fullUrl/version uniqueness rules used as a comparison target. The parameters-fullUrl extension now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack, and current core source correctly links to it through the extensions-location macro. FHIR-I 2018-07-09 minutes list FHIR-17406 as Persuasive, and no substantive conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit is needed because current authoritative source already answers the implementer question: duplicate parameter.resource ids are not automatically the same resource/version in bare Parameters, ambiguity is noted, Bundle uniqueness guidance is linked, and Bundle identity rules apply only when a fullUrl is supplied.

Added adjacent Parameters reference-resolution guidance in the same table.
